sections.title: Logos, tracks & motifs
paragraphs: Do: Pick the variant by background, not by taste. Color lockups on white and light neutrals. All-white on navy, on the accent color, or on busy photography. Reverse (white wordmark + accent NEXT) only on navy or near-black.
Do: Hold the clear space. Minimum clear space on all four sides equals the cap height of the word NEXT in the lockup. Nothing — type, rules, image edges, other logos — enters that zone.
Do: Respect minimum sizes. Side-by-side lockups: 180 px / 45 mm minimum width. Stacked lockups: 96 px / 25 mm minimum width. Below that, use the NEXT 26 wordmark alone.

Do: Use the supplied vectors. EPS or AI for print and fabrication, SVG for screen, PNG only when transparency is required and vectors are impossible. Never re-trace, re-typeset or screenshot a lockup.
Don't: Never recolor a lockup. Each division accent is fixed. Do not tint the navy, apply gradients, or borrow another division's accent for a lockup.
Don't: Never rebuild or re-space the lockup. Do not change the gap between the division name and NEXT, restack a side-by-side lockup, or set the division name in a different weight.
Don't: Never distort, rotate or add effects. No stretching, skewing, arcing, drop shadows, bevels, outlines or keylines. Scale proportionally only.
Don't: Never place a color lockup on a low-contrast field. Navy on a dark photo or the Learn yellow on white both fail. Switch to the all-white lockup or add an approved scrim.
Don't: Never mix two division lockups in one lockup zone. Where two tracks appear together, use the master TransPerfect NEXT lockup and name the tracks in type.

sections.title: Grounds, resizing & reuse
paragraphs: Do: Use one ground per sign family so a set reads as one look across the venue.
Do: Run one continuous ramp across pieces that stand together — stair tiers, booth front and sides, door pairs.
Do: Put the white lockup and headline on the dark end of the ramp.
Don't: Don't set text on the lightest stops, or add a second gradient on top of a ground.
Don't: Don't convert a ground to CMYK yourself — use the measured builds or the printer's approved build.
Sizes come from the venue's site survey only — never from artwork sizes or guesses.
The background stretches to the new trim plus ⅛ in bleed; it is never tiled or cropped by hand.
Logos, text and arrows keep their own size and stay at the same relative position on the sign.
Pieces only ever shrink to fit the new safe area; they never grow past the designer's size.
Turned headlines turn around their anchor, so they stay centred where the designer centred them.
Each new size is saved as its own version; the supplied original never changes.
Digital formats switch layout by shape (wide, square, tall…), not by stretching one design.
copy: Ground, lockup position, type sizes, arrows and print rules.
change: Wording, the division logo, and the size (from the survey).
never: Colours, the lockup itself, and supplied CMYK builds.

Pack · aqua → violet: #B2E1F5 → #8ECEE7 → #64AAD3 → #5373B9 → #5342A2 → #542E96. The house scenic ground of the delivery — exterior flags, lift walls and doors, Paolozzi and Mountbatten set wraps, Wall 4E, pillar wraps, metal logo wall, Churchill double doors. Carries a measured black shade through the middle of the run, which is what keeps the mid-tones from going chalky on vinyl.

Pack · orchid → blue: #BC7DC5 → #B17FC6 → #8A7FC7 → #5586C5 → #1E84C1. Front-of-house desk ground: registration desk fronts and sides, cloakroom, catering table, help desks. Runs orchid into brand blue with no black at all, so long low panels stay clean under downlighting.

Pack · cyan → pink: #0C8CC6 → #268BCA → #6097D0 → #9C8FCD → #F573C0. Glass and screen-surround ground from the Churchill booth vinyls: a saturated cyan field turning through to pink. Widest hue travel in the delivery — used where a panel is seen against daylight.

Beam · violet → aqua: #542E96 → #5342A2 → #5373B9 → #64AAD3 → #B2E1F5. Hero treatment, on the delivery's house scenic ground run at full travel: violet head into aqua. Used on the Churchill demo columns and the Whittle stage wings.

Wash · diagonal: #5373B9 → #64AAD3 → #8ECEE7 → #B2E1F5. Low-energy diagonal wash for long horizontal runs (coffee bars, merch mart, stage fascias): the light half of the house scenic ground, so a 4 m panel holds no visible turn.

Horizon: #BC7DC5 → #B17FC6 → #8A7FC7 → #5586C5 → #1E84C1. The delivery's front-of-house desk ground — orchid into brand blue, no black in the build. Reads calmly behind help-desk copy and wide desk fronts, exactly as the registration desk vinyls print.
Bloom · corner: #542E96 → #5342A2 → #64AAD3 → #B2E1F5. Corner bloom that anchors a panel to its neighbour, on the house scenic ground. Used inside the Flemming LED surround set.

Prism sweep: #0C8CC6 → #268BCA → #6097D0 → #9C8FCD → #F573C0. The Churchill glass-vinyl ground: saturated cyan turning through to pink, the widest hue travel in the delivery. Reserved for the merch mart and the Westminster/Cambridge screens.

Chevron sweep: #14142D → #542E96 → #5373B9 → #8ECEE7. Low-angle brand sweep for cloakroom, help-desk and close-up square panels: brand navy head into the house scenic ground, so a white lockup keeps full contrast at arm's length.
Dawn: #64AAD3 → #8ECEE7 → #B2E1F5. Lightest ground in the pack — the aqua end of the house scenic ramp on its own. Default for plinths, tall surrounds and the Whittle centre panels.
Veil: #8ECEE7 → #64AAD3. Near-flat veil for slivers and thin fascia strips where a gradient would band: two adjacent stops of the house scenic ramp.

Brew · diagonal: #14142D → #244299 → #1E84C1 → #8ECEE7. NEXTbrew ground: a deep diagonal run out of brand navy through brand blue into the delivery's aqua, themed with a live café motif — cup rings, steam ribbons and a bean tick row, all editable vector marks in the masters. The darker head end keeps the white lockup at full contrast under warm café lighting.
Repeat wash: #14142D → #542E96 → #5373B9. Deep vertical wash sized for step-and-repeat walls, so the tiled lockup rows stay legible in on-camera flash.

Repeat · white: #FFFFFF → #FBFCFE → #F2F5FA. Near-white press-wall ground for the full-colour division lockup wall. Keeps every division colourway at its approved value with no gradient tint under flash.
Stair ramp: #03002C → #003FC7. One ramp across every tier of a stair wrap: tier 1 (bottom) takes the dark end, the top tier the bright end, so the run reads as one flowing gradient.
Violet to blue: #CE78E8 → #9B6FE2 → #3F5BCE → #2B54C9 → #9B6FE2 → #CE78E8. Delegate guide and booklet pages.
Violet to blue, quiet: #D7A0EE → #A98AE6 → #5C74D6 → #A98AE6 → #D7A0EE. Delegate guide and booklet pages.
Deep navy: #002442 → #001A31. Delegate guide and booklet pages.
White paper: #FFFFFF → #FFFFFF. Delegate guide and booklet pages.

Division accent ramp: #13b1f3 → #5ce1e6 → #a6fa87 → #ffeb66 → #ff9b70 → #ec388a → #c2a3ff. The order division accents run in when several appear together. For fills, rules and icons — never body text.

sections.title: Official logo & usage
paragraphs: Use the artwork exactly as supplied — never redraw, stretch, recolour or crop the badge.
Light backgrounds: use the main full-colour logo.
Dark backgrounds: use the white outline version (the dark-background variant).
Single colour: when we get to choose the one colour, navy is preferred.
If only black and white are available, use the black version on light backgrounds and the white version on dark backgrounds.
Keep clear space around the badge of at least x on every side, where x is the full height of the ribbon element, navy outline included (171.7 units, 14.47% of the logo width).
Don't place the badge over busy photography or patterns that fight the artwork.
Print: 40 mm wide. Keeps the 7.8-unit keyline at 0.26 mm; at 25 mm it drops to 0.16 mm and the lace and letter details to 0.07 mm, below what presses hold.

Screen: 160 px wide. Every line stays at or above 1 px. Below 160 px the detail fills in on every version, including single colour — use the small-size mark files (the same badge, trimmed and pre-sized) and check legibility.

Embroidery / patch (full colour): 90 mm wide. Stitching needs about 1 mm per detail; at 60 mm the keyline is 0.39 mm. One-colour embroidery can go to 60 mm with a digitiser stitch-out (see Single colour).
Don't stretch or squash: The badge always keeps its supplied proportions.

Don't recolour: No tints, gradients or new colours. One-colour use only as shown on the Single colour page: the supplied Navy, Black and White files, or an event-colour ink signed off by the designer.
Don't crop: The whole diamond stays visible, banner to waves.
Don't rotate: The badge sits upright on its point, never tilted.
Don't use busy backgrounds: No photography or patterns that fight the artwork.
Don't lose contrast: Full colour never sits on Caribbean Sky or similar mid-tones.
Don't add effects: No drop shadows, glows, bevels or outlines on the resting logo. Motion graphics may use light and shadow for depth while the badge moves.
Don't retype the lettering: The words inside the badge are artwork, not live text.

sections.title: Colour balance & readable pairings
paragraphs: HEX, RGB and HSL values are exact, taken from the supplied artwork — use them as-is on screen and web.
CMYK values are the inks set in the master EPS/AI files, so they match what the vector files print. They are not proofed: always run a vendor proof before print and adjust on press if needed.
